why: The 300 MW project triggers a federal Title V major-source operating permit because the computed NOx potential to emit of 1,067 tpy (based on the assumption of 121 N+1 diesel generators of 2,500 kW each operating 500 hours per year at 6.4 g/kWh NOx) exceeds the 100 tpy threshold per 40 CFR 70.2. The same 300 MW load exceeds the 75 MW threshold in Texas SB 6, invoking large-load interconnection standards with a computed margin of 225 MW per the bill text. Additionally, the Governor's data center interconnection audit applies because the 300 MW load exceeds the 75 MW ERCOT large-load threshold, and the directive states the audit must be completed before any data center project moves forward. All three rules are graded major, indicating significant permitting, interconnection, and audit requirements that do not outright block the project but impose substantial process steps. Therefore, the verdict is conditional on satisfying these federal and state requirements.

state_watch.bill: Governor Abbott August 3, 2026 Data Center Audit Directive
state_watch.status: Governor directive issued 2026-08-03; ERCOT implementation notice issued 2026-08-03.
state_watch.key_provisions: Directs PUCT and ERCOT to verify and audit every data center advancing through ERCOT interconnection before it may move forward, pausing the Batch Zero process pending the required review.

state_watch.status: Passed Senate 2025-03-19 (with amendments); passed House 2025-05-27 (RV#3643); Senate concurred in House amendments 2025-05-29; signed by Governor 2025-06-20, effective immediately.
state_watch.key_provisions: Requires PUCT/ERCOT large-load planning and interconnection standards; applies to large loads at a default 75 MW single-site threshold; addresses interconnection studies, cost allocation, co-location, and emergency curtailment
